# Bintje (01, engineer) — SPD-039

## Brief
Objective: a redirection or tee target that zsh reads as a glob using its own operators, parenthesised alternation `(a|b)` and the numeric range `<n-m>` (also `<->`, `<n->`, `<-m>`), is captured as the word zsh opens and checked as every file it can open, so a member cannot write a protected file through one (Laws 1 and 5). Where the hook cannot tell what zsh opens, it refuses a member and checks Spud against every possibility. Red-first.

The hole (proposal 32 from SPUD-034/Atlantic; `spud ticket show SPD-039` has the evidence): shell_tokens and separate_redirects use shlex punctuation, so in `echo x > (ledger|x)/tickets/SPD-001.md` the `(` starts a subshell and the captured target is `/tickets/SPD-001.md`, and in `echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-<1-1>.md` the `<` becomes an input redirection and the target is `ledger/tickets/SPD-`; each maps outside the protected roots and a `**` member's write is silent, while zsh 5.9 writes ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md (and every match of an open range). bash rejects both as syntax errors, so the divergence is zsh-only.

Settle with real-shell probes (zsh -f, zsh with the options of the Bash tool's shell on this Mac, which sets `nobareglobqual`, and bash 3.2; in the scratchpad) and pin each with a test:
1. Where zsh reads `(` and `<` as glob syntax rather than punctuation: inside or at the start of a redirection target word, a tee argument, a word after a command name; `<n-m>` only when it matches the range form; `(` only where a word can continue. Tokenize so that in those positions the word zsh sees is kept whole, without changing how bash-valid lines tokenize (every existing test stays green). If the tokenizer cannot do this without a large rewrite, the safe fallback is detection: a target position followed by `(`, or a `<` glued to a word that forms a range, makes the target unknown (refused for a member, every reading checked for Spud). State which you chose and why.
2. Expansion: extend SPD-034's bounded matcher (bounded_glob, brace_expand, neutralize_quoted_globs, deglob) to alternation (nested, with `/` not allowed inside a group in zsh; probe it) and numeric ranges (open ends, leading zeros), under the same scan and match caps. Quoted operators stay literal.
3. Qualifiers and flags: with bareglobqual on (zsh default) a trailing `(.)`, `(/)`, `(N)` is a glob qualifier and `(N)` turns on nullglob for that pattern; on this Mac's Bash tool it is off. Decide how the hook treats a trailing parenthesised group (both readings checked, or refused for a member) and pin it. `(#i)`, `^`, `~` need extendedglob, which is off here; keep them under SPD-034's documented limit unless the fix covers them for free.
4. cd targets: SPD-030 makes a glob cd target unfollowable; check that `cd (ledger|x)` and `cd SPD-<1-2>` are unfollowable too rather than mis-tokenized into a subshell or redirection.
5. The same words in command position (`(cd x)`, `cmd <file`) keep their current meaning; bash-only lines (`cat <(git push)`, `diff <(a) <(b)`, `>(tee x)`) keep SPD-030's handling.

Out of scope: writes by arbitrary programs, cd into an unenterable directory (SPD-037, next), Spud's relative redirection after an unfollowable cd (SPD-035), extendedglob and bash extglob patterns beyond what item 3 decides, native rules (SPD-033). File a proposal for anything else larger you find.

Deliverables (only these paths): `bin/**`, `tests/**`. Never `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `ledger/`, `reports/`, `docs/`.

Read first: `spud ticket show SPD-039`; `spud member show SPUD-034/Atlantic` (the expander and its decisions); `spud member show SPUD-030/Elba` (the tokenizer and ShellWalk); `spud member show SPUD-036/Huckleberry` (the review corpus); in bin/spud_ledger.py: `shell_tokens`, `separate_redirects`, `newlines_as_separators`, `split_substitutions`, `ShellWalk`, `analyse_segment`, `neutralize_quoted_globs`, `deglob`, `brace_expand`, `bounded_glob`, `cd_target`, `bash_reason`; tests/test_hooks.py `GlobRedirectTest`, `ShellModelTest`, `BashHookCase`; tests/helpers.py.

Constraints: the hook budget holds: measure PreToolUse(Bash) median of 15 before and after, same payloads (a plain redirection, an alternation redirection, a git write), interleaved with a scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin/, and put both numbers in the result. The live hooks run the ledger root's bin/spud on main, not this worktree's copy; probe with a scratch SPUD_HOME as the tests do, never against the live ledger. Shell probes that write run in a scratchpad directory only, never with a pattern that can match a real repository file. The live Bash hook refuses git writes for you and any command naming the ledger state directory, and the harness may refuse shell text naming git that it cannot show stays in the worktree: put such payloads inside Python test code. Run the suite from this worktree in the background: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (485 tests, about three minutes). Any `claude -p` probe passes `--model haiku`.

Done when: tests in tests/test_hooks.py that failed on the unchanged code now pass, covering the ticket's two evidence commands and the open range for a `**` member, a narrow-glob member and Spud; nested alternation; a range with leading zeros; tee arguments; a trailing qualifier-shaped group as decided; the cd cases; and controls that stay as they are: `(cd x)`, `cmd <file`, `cat <(...)`, a quoted `(a|b)` in a deliverable target, an alternation matching only deliverables, `2>&1`, `> /dev/null`. The whole suite is green; latency and every decision with its shell probe are in the result.

## Sub-agents

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: a read-write redirection <> opens its target for writing but is skipped as input** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-040]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: IN_REDIRECTS holds <>, so separate_redirects drops its operand unchecked; <> opens the file O_RDWR, and 1<>file lets the command overwrite it from the start without truncation. A member can write any protected file (Laws 1 and 5) silently. Found in SPD-039 probing; outside its brief (zsh glob operators).
  Evidence: Probe zsh 5.9 -f and -o nobareglobqual in a scratchpad: echo x 1<>ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md over a file holding orig left x then ig, the file changed. analyse_command on that line records no redirect (redirects []), so bash_reason checks nothing. bash 3.2 supports n<> the same way. Fix sketch: treat <> (with or without an fd prefix) as an output redirection in separate_redirects, keeping its operand as a target.
- **Bash hook: a glob in the command word or a git verb hides the command (Law 7)** — suggested P1; created as [[SPD-041]] at P1 by Spud.
  Why: analyse_segment takes the command word and git verb as spelled. Both shells expand an unquoted glob there before running it, so a member can run a git write through a path glob such as /usr/bin/g?t or a zsh alternation g(i|x)t, or a verb glob matching a file it created (touch push, then p?sh). SPD-034 expands globs only in redirection and tee targets; SPD-039 only fixes zsh operators in targets. Outside SPD-039's brief.
  Evidence: analyse_command reads /usr/bin/g?t push and /usr/bin/g(i|x)t push as kind other with no git finding (SPD-039 scratchpad). Probe zsh 5.9 -o nobareglobqual: /bin/ech(o) hello ran /bin/echo and printed hello; with bareglobqual (o) is read as a qualifier and errors, but an alternation such as (i|x) is a group under both options. Fix sketch: when the command word or the git verb holds an active glob (GLOB_RE, or SPD-039's zsh sentinels), refuse a member (an unresolvable command word, like a variable) or expand it against PATH and the candidate directories within the SPD-034 budget.
- **Bash hook: zsh short loop forms hide their body (repeat N cmd, for x (list) cmd)** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-042]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: zsh's SHORT_LOOPS, on by default, runs a loop body without do and done. ShellWalk pushes a loop frame on for, select and repeat and skips the header words until do, so in repeat 3 cmd and for f (a b) cmd the body is read as header and discarded: a member's git write or redirection there is not checked (Laws 1, 5, 7). zsh only; bash has no such forms. Found in SPD-039, outside its brief.
  Evidence: Probe zsh 5.9 -f and -o nobareglobqual in a scratchpad: repeat 2 echo r >> out, repeat 1 (echo rs >> out), for f (a b) echo $f >> out, for f in a b; echo $f >> out, foreach f (a b); ...; end, while (( n++ < 2 )) { ... } and if [[ -n x ]] echo i >> out all wrote out. analyse_command (unchanged SPD-038 bin) records no redirect for repeat 3 echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md, repeat 1 (echo x > ledger/...) or for f (a b) echo x > ledger/...; for f in a b; cmd and foreach were read. Fix sketch: after repeat N, and after a for header closed by a parenthesised list, read what follows as a loop body (loop_depth) rather than header.

## Result
Produced (worktree spd-039-zsh-glob-operators, uncommitted): bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py only.

THE FIX. A redirection or tee target that zsh reads as a glob with its own operators, parenthesised alternation (a|b) and the numeric range <n-m> (<->, <n->, <-m>), is now kept whole and expanded, and every file it can open is checked. Before, shlex split it into a subshell or an input redirection, and the hook checked a fragment that mapped under no root.
- mark_zsh_patterns, a text pass after neutralize_quoted_globs, marks the characters zsh reads as pattern syntax with private-use sentinels, following zsh's command-position rules as probed. A group opening a word outside command position is marked; so is a group glued inside a word and a range anywhere. Left as before: subshells in command position, case patterns, [[ ]], (( )), $((, name=(...) arrays, ${...}, heredoc delimiters, quoted or escaped parentheses, and groups holding ; & > or a non-range <.
- When the pass changes a line, analyse_command walks two readings: zsh's first, then the other shell's. The second restores ranges (bash: two redirections) and groups that open a word (shlex reading, a subshell where a shell runs one); glued groups stay whole there, since neither shell runs them. Every finding and target of either reading is checked; cwds and variables after the line are the union.
- The expander (SPD-034's bounded matcher) reads a group as an alternation and a range as an exact numeric regex (numeric_range_regex, leading zeros allowed, open ends). A group holding / or left open opens nothing (zsh: bad pattern). A trailing group with no | is expanded both as qualifiers (the rest of the pattern) and as a group. cd_target sees the sentinels via GLOB_RE, so a cd into a pattern is unfollowable.
- Code in qualifiers (e, oe, e{...}, e[...], +name) is analysed as commands run in a loop in the expanding shell.
- Hardening: one pass pairs parens and braces, so group reading is linear (unbalanced opens were quadratic). Substitution bodies are analysed once per starting state (analyse_isolated memo). The regex compile falls back to any name on RecursionError. The line is tokenized once.

DECISIONS, each with its probe (zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual = this Mac's Bash tool, bash 3.2; scratchpad fixtures only):
1. Tokenize, not detect (item 1). Probe: in zsh, ( starts a word as a pattern after a command word, after a spaced redirection operator, after &> and >|, and in for lists; mid-word always. It is a subshell at command start and after time, !, if, {, |, an assignment, and a leading redirection's target. A range is a glob at any position, command position included (<1-2> 2>&1: no matches found). Glued >( and 2>( stay process substitution; >>( is an error. Inside a group, blanks are part of the word; ; & < > make a parse error and the whole eval runs nothing. bash: ( there is a syntax error; <1-1> is < 1-1 >, and cat <1-2> out writes out. Detection alone would have lost Spud's every-reading check and bash's range reading, hence two readings. Probe 5: a ( glued to a reserved word in command position is a subshell in bash (!(, {(, if(, time(, then(, do(, else( ran) and in zsh ({(, else(). f()(body) is a subshell body in both; time -p ( and coproc NAME ( are bash subshells, repeat 1 ( a zsh one. So those are never marked, () keeps command position, and word-start groups keep the second reading.
2. Expansion (item 2). Probes: SPD-<1-1>.md wrote SPD-001.md; <-> wrote SPD-001, 002 and 010; <2-> wrote 002 and 010; <-1> wrote 001; <001-002> wrote both; tests/<7-7> matched tests/007; tests/<1-1>/../../ledger/... wrote the ledger file; 1<-> does not match 1; <2-1> matches nothing (read as ordered: more checked). Nested ((ledger|y)|x) and SPD-(<1-1>|zz).md wrote. (ledger/tickets|x) is a bad pattern (nothing opened; a member gets "matches no file"). Quoted "(a|b)" and escaped \(a\|b\) stay literal.
3. Trailing qualifier-shaped group (item 3). Probe: with bareglobqual, SPD-001.md(.) and (N) wrote the file and (/) matched nothing; with nobareglobqual (this Mac) (.) is a group and matched nothing. Decision: check both readings' files. Also with bareglobqual, (e:"touch ran":), (oe:...:), (e{...}), (e[...]) and (+f) ran code, and a cd there moved the command's directory; the hook reads each string as commands in a loop. extendedglob (#q), ^, ~ and bash extglob stay under SPD-034's documented limit.
4. cd (item 4). Probe: zsh followed cd (ledger|y), pushd (ledger|y) and cd SPD-<1-2>; bash errors. They are now unfollowable: a member's relative target after one is refused ("cannot follow"); before, the hook read a cd to the home directory beside a subshell.
5. Command position (item 5). (cd x), cmd <file, cat <(...), diff <(a) <(b), >(tee x), case (x|y) patterns, f() {...}, arrays, $(( )), (( )) and [[ ( ) ]] leave the line unchanged (one reading, as before).

TESTS, red first: ZshGlobOperatorTest, 15 methods (two, the reserved-word subshell test and the pathological-input test, were added while refining and hardening). On the unchanged code, 13 of the first 13 ran with 33 failures and 1 error. Coverage: evidence alternation for the ** member, the tests/** member and Spud; the evidence range, plus the range in a directory component (hole for all three); open ranges; nesting; the unreadable group; the range matcher against brute force (0 to 1199, zero-padded); tee; qualifier readings; qualifier code; cd; bash's range reading; reserved-word subshells; pathological inputs; linear nested substitutions; controls ((cd x), cmd <file, cat <(git push), diff <(..) <(..), a quoted (a|b) deliverable target, an alternation matching only deliverables, 2>&1, > /dev/null, spud allow with a quoted group). Full suite from the worktree: Ran 500 tests, OK (485 before; a first run at 499 was green before hardening).

VERIFIED BEYOND TESTS. A differential of old against new analyse_command over 470 command lines extracted from tests/test_hooks.py: 33 read differently, all zsh-pattern lines. 13 lose something: only shlex fragments of lines bash rejects (tests/, tests/keep., ~+/) and subshell kinds of glued groups; no git, spud, database or variable finding lost. 15 pathological inputs: none raise or hang; 500KB word with a group 1.9 s against 1.7 s unchanged; 40000 unbalanced opens bounded.

LATENCY, PreToolUse(Bash) median of 15, interleaved with the scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin, same scratch home and bound member: plain redirection 22.0 to 22.4 ms (silent both); alternation redirection 22.0 to 22.9 ms (silent before, deny now); git write 22.2 to 22.6 ms (deny both). Unchanged within a millisecond.

PROPOSALS filed (held by Spud): 33 (P1) read-write redirection <> skipped as input, although 1<>ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md overwrote the file in the probe. 34 (P1) a glob in the command word or git verb hides the command (/usr/bin/g?t push, /usr/bin/g(i|x)t push read as other). 35 (P2) zsh short loop forms hide their body (repeat 3 cmd, for f (a b) cmd; probed, the walk records nothing).

LIMITS: for a group that opens a word, the second reading still checks shlex's fragments (the text after the closing parenthesis), which can refuse a member conservatively; option-gated patterns stay as in SPD-034. CLAUDE.md suite count becomes 500. No subagents used. Branch ready for review (Spud's call).

## Outcome
zsh's (a|b) alternation and <n-m> ranges in a redirection or tee target are kept whole by mark_zsh_patterns and expanded by SPD-034's bounded matcher; when the pass changes a line both the zsh and the bash readings are walked and every finding checked. A trailing qualifier-shaped group is checked both ways and qualifier code (e, oe, +f) is analysed as commands; a cd into such a pattern is unfollowable. The real range hole was a range in a directory component, silent for all callers. Hardened deep nesting and quadratic unbalanced parens. ZshGlobOperatorTest 15 methods, 33 failures red first; a 470-line differential lost no git, spud or database finding; suite 500 OK, rerun by Spud; latency within a millisecond. Proposals 33, 34, 35 became SPD-040 (P1), SPD-041 (P1), SPD-042 (P2).
